journey.note: Tribunal took Rs 55,500 a month, less 10% tax, plus 50% future prospects, half deduction, multiplier 18; 9% interest from the date the detailed accident report was filed with the tribunal (Sept 2013). No consortium.
Cross-appeals by the insurer (negligence, excess) and the parents (enhancement) both dismissed; award kept in full.
Insurer's appeal dismissed; parents' appeal partly allowed: Rs 40,000 filial consortium to each parent added, with interest as awarded by the tribunal.

precedent.holding: Hitting a stationary truck from behind does not by itself prove the car driver negligent. For a professional student, income cannot rest on assumed career success or unrelated professionals' salaries. Adding future prospects to an already forward-looking income overlaps, though the Court did not cut the award. An omitted filial consortium head must be added.

extraction.family_summary: A 20-year-old chartered accountancy student died in 2013 when the car he was in hit a truck left standing on a dark Delhi road without lights or warning signs. The tribunal awarded Rs 81,21,900 in 2017, and the High Court kept that amount in 2022 after appeals by both the insurer and his parents. In 2026 the Supreme Court rejected the insurer's appeal and refused to value his income on a qualified CA's salary, but added Rs 80,000 for the parents' loss of their son's company, making Rs 82,01,900 with 9% interest, 13 years after the accident.
what_mattered: The truck driver and owner never gave evidence, and the injured car driver's account of an unlit truck stood, so the claim that the car driver was to blame failed.

The tribunal used an entry-level government officer's pay (Rs 55,500 a month), not his small stipend, and still added 50% for future prospects. The Supreme Court saw this as an overlap but would not cut it after 13 years, nor raise it on qualified CAs' salaries or unproved tuition income.
Both lower courts gave the parents nothing for losing their son's love and company (filial consortium); the Supreme Court added Rs 40,000 for each parent.
